rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with the provided 3AA label, but the image itself does not clearly support a confident statement of a dense upper-quadrant ICM, circumferential AA trophectoderm, or a blastocoel occupying most of the embryo; some visual details appear overstated.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, male factor diagnosis, prior biochemical pregnancy, sperm parameters, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with clear linkage from embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis, though some quantitative adjustments and causal emphasis on alcohol/endometrial thickness are stronger than the evidence clearly supports.

Core points are guideline-consistent (good prognosis with young age and high-grade blastocyst, proceed with transfer, lifestyle counseling), but recommendations such as ERA, thrombophilia screening, NK/immunologic testing, and broad workup after only one biochemical pregnancy are not strongly guideline-supported.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including counseling and possible uterine evaluation, though some suggested tests are more aggressive than typically indicated for this history.
